deeds.name: 5 Obligatory Prayers (Fard)
deeds.description: The five daily prayers, the foundational pillar of Islam.
howToDo: Pray Fajr (2 rak'ahs), Dhuhr (4), Asr (4), Maghrib (3), and Isha (4) within their prescribed time windows.
Fulfill every compulsory pillar and act within each prayer with focus and humility.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Serves as the foundational pillar of Islam, purifies daily sins between prayers, and maintains continuous divine connection.

references.text: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
The deed most beloved to Allah is prayer performed at its proper time.

deeds.name: Congregational Prayer in Mosque
deeds.description: Pray the five daily prayers behind the Imam at the mosque.
howToDo: Make wudu and walk to the masjid ahead of the prayer time.
Stand in rows behind the Imam and complete the obligatory prayer together with fellow worshipers.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Multiplies the reward of prayer 27 times, fosters brotherhood, and secures divine protection.

references.text: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times superior to prayer performed individually.

deeds.name: Praying Fajr & Isha in Congregation
deeds.description: Attend the mosque specifically for Fajr and Isha prayers.
howToDo: Attend the mosque for the dawn (Fajr) congregational prayer.
Return for the late-night (Isha) congregational prayer.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Equivalent to standing in voluntary night prayer all night long, builds self-discipline, and guards against hypocrisy.

references.text: Whoever prays Isha in congregation, it is as if he prayed half the night, and whoever prays Fajr in congregation, it is as if he prayed the entire night.

deeds.name: 12 Raka'at Sunnah Rawatib
deeds.description: The twelve confirmed rak'ahs prayed around the five daily prayers.
howToDo: Pray 2 rak'ahs before Fajr.
Pray 4 rak'ahs before Dhuhr (as 2+2) and 2 rak'ahs after.
Pray 2 rak'ahs after Maghrib and 2 rak'ahs after Isha.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Guarantees a house built by Allah in Paradise and compensates for minor deficiencies in the obligatory prayers.

references.text: Whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day and a night will have a house built for him in Paradise.

deeds.name: Sunnah Before Fajr (2 Raka'at)
deeds.description: Two light rak'ahs prayed right after the Fajr adhan.
howToDo: Perform 2 light rak'ahs immediately after the Fajr adhan.
Recite Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Better than the entire world and everything in it; instills early morning peace and spiritual clarity.

references.text: The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.

deeds.name: Witr Prayer
deeds.description: An odd-numbered prayer that closes out the night.
howToDo: Pray an odd number of rak'ahs (1, 3, or 5) as the final prayer of the night.
Perform it either right after Isha or as the very last prayer before sleep or dawn.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Fulfills a beloved Sunnah, since Allah is odd and loves the odd, ensuring your day finishes in devotion.

references.text: Make Witr the last of your prayer at night.
Allah is Witr (One) and loves the Witr, so perform Witr, O people of the Qur'an.

deeds.name: Tahajjud (Night Vigil Prayer)
deeds.description: Voluntary night prayer performed after waking, before Fajr.
howToDo: Wake up in the last third of the night and make wudu.
Pray 2 to 8 voluntary rak'ahs, in sets of two.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Brings one closest to Allah during the Divine Descent, ensures answered supplications, and grants spiritual light (nur).

references.text: Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and He says: Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?

deeds.name: Duha Prayer (Forenoon Prayer)
deeds.description: A short prayer after sunrise, standing in for daily charity.
howToDo: Wait until about 15-20 minutes after sunrise.
Pray 2, 4, 6, or 8 rak'ahs any time before Dhuhr.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Fulfills the daily charity due upon all 360 joints of the body and brings blessing in livelihood.

references.text: In the morning, charity is due on every joint bone of the body of every one of you... and two rak'ahs which one prays in the forenoon will suffice for that.

deeds.name: Tahiyyatul Masjid (Greeting Mosque)
deeds.description: Two light rak'ahs prayed immediately upon entering a mosque.
howToDo: Upon entering a mosque, pray 2 light rak'ahs before sitting down.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Demonstrates proper reverence for the house of Allah, converting physical entry into instant worship.

references.text: When any one of you enters the mosque, he should not sit down until he has prayed two rak'ahs.

deeds.name: Tahiyyatul Wudu (Prayer After Wudu)
deeds.description: Two voluntary rak'ahs prayed shortly after ablution.
howToDo: Shortly after completing wudu, pray 2 voluntary rak'ahs with focus and humility.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Erases prior minor sins and serves as a direct path to Paradise, as exemplified by Bilal (RA).

references.text: I have never purified myself with an ablution, at any hour of night or day, without praying with that purification whatever was written for me to pray, said Bilal, when asked by the Prophet about his most hopeful deed in Islam.

deeds.name: Salat al-Istikhara (Guidance)
deeds.description: Two rak'ahs prayed for guidance before a decision.
howToDo: When facing a decision, pray 2 non-obligatory rak'ahs.
Follow with the prescribed Istikhara supplication, then proceed with an open heart.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Eliminates anxiety, aligns choices with divine decree, and entrusts outcomes to Allah.

references.text: O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty.

deeds.name: Salat al-Tawbah (Repentance)
deeds.description: Two rak'ahs prayed with sincere repentance.
howToDo: Perform proper wudu and pray 2 rak'ahs.
Sincerely ask Allah for forgiveness while resolving to leave the sin behind.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Erases committed sins, purifies the heart, and re-establishes divine mercy.

references.text: There is no man who commits a sin, then gets up and purifies himself, then prays two rak'ahs, then asks forgiveness of Allah, but Allah forgives him.

deeds.name: Jumu'ah (Friday) Prayer
deeds.description: The obligatory Friday congregational prayer and khutbah.
howToDo: Perform ghusl and arrive early at the masjid.
Listen attentively to the khutbah, then pray 2 rak'ahs with the Imam.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Wipes away sins committed between Fridays and unites the Muslim community in weekly remembrance.

references.text: O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
Whoever performs ghusl on Friday like the ghusl for major impurity and then goes early to the mosque is as if he had sacrificed a camel.

deeds.name: Salat al-Kusuf / Khusuf (Eclipse)
deeds.preferredTime: During a solar or lunar eclipse
deeds.description: A special prayer performed during a solar or lunar eclipse.
howToDo: During a solar or lunar eclipse, pray 2 rak'ahs.
Perform two bowings (ruku') within each rak'ah with long recitation.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Instills awe of Allah's cosmic power, reminds of the Day of Judgment, and prompts repentance.

references.text: The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah. They do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone, but when you see that, remember Allah.

deeds.name: Salat al-Janazah (Funeral Prayer)
deeds.preferredTime: Whenever a funeral prayer is held
deeds.description: The communal funeral prayer, a collective obligation.
howToDo: Stand in rows without ruku' or sujud.
Say four Takbirs, reciting Al-Fatihah, Salawat, a du'a for the deceased, and closing Taslim.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Earns a reward equivalent to a mountain of Uhud and fulfills a vital communal obligation.

references.text: Whoever attends the funeral until the prayer is offered will have a reward of one qirat, and whoever attends until burial will have a reward of two qirats, each qirat like the great mountain of Uhud.
The smallest of the two qirats is like the mountain of Uhud.

deeds.name: Sajdah al-Tilawah (Prostration)
deeds.preferredTime: Whenever a prostration verse is recited
deeds.description: A single prostration upon reciting or hearing a verse of prostration.
howToDo: Upon reading or hearing a verse of prostration, perform a single prostration.
Glorify Allah during the prostration, then rise.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Demonstrates immediate submission to revelation and causes Satan to weep in despair.

references.text: When the son of Adam recites a verse of prostration and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping, saying: Woe to me, the son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so his is Paradise, and I was commanded to prostrate and I refused, so mine is the Fire.

deeds.name: Sajdah al-Shukr (Thanks Prostration)
deeds.description: A prostration of gratitude upon receiving good news.
howToDo: Upon receiving joyful news or being saved from calamity, prostrate immediately.
Give thanks to Allah during the prostration.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Cultivates deep humility, preserves blessings from vanishing, and draws one closer to Allah.

references.text: Whenever a matter that would bring him joy came to him, or he was given glad tidings, the Prophet would fall down in prostration, thanking Allah.

deeds.name: Recite Al-Qur'an (Any Surah)
deeds.description: Recite any portion of the Qur'an with focus and sincerity.
howToDo: Read any portion or chapter of the Qur'an with proper Tajweed.
Recite with focus and sincerity, even a small consistent portion.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Earns ten rewards per letter, softens the heart, and brings spiritual healing (shifa') to the soul.

references.text: Whoever reads a letter from the Book of Allah, he will have a reward, and that reward will be multiplied by ten. I do not say that Alif Lam Mim is a letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter.

deeds.name: Recite Surah Al-Kahf on Friday
deeds.description: Recite Surah Al-Kahf between Thursday sunset and Friday sunset.
howToDo: Recite Surah Al-Kahf (Chapter 18) any time between Thursday sunset and Friday sunset.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Casts light for the reciter between the two Fridays and shields against the tribulations of Dajjal.

references.text: Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on the day of Friday, light will shine for him between the two Fridays.
Whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal.

deeds.name: Recite Surah Al-Mulk Before Sleep
deeds.description: Recite Surah Al-Mulk every night before sleeping.
howToDo: Recite Surah Al-Mulk (Chapter 67) every night before sleeping.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Intercedes continuously for the reader until forgiven and protects against the torment of the grave.

references.text: There is a surah in the Qur'an of thirty verses which will intercede for its companion until he is forgiven: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Tabarak alladhi bi yadihil-mulk).

deeds.name: Recite Ayatul Kursi After Fard Salah
deeds.description: Recite Ayat al-Kursi once after every obligatory prayer.
howToDo: Recite Ayat al-Kursi (Al-Baqarah 2:255) once immediately after each obligatory prayer.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Ensures that the only barrier between the reciter and entering Paradise is physical death.

references.text: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi immediately after every obligatory prayer, nothing stands between him and entering Paradise except death.
The greatest verse in the Book of Allah is Ayat al-Kursi.

deeds.name: Recite 3 Quls Nightly
deeds.description: Recite the three Quls and wipe them over the body before sleep.
howToDo: Cup your hands and recite Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas.
Blow into your hands and wipe them across your body; repeat three times.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Provides complete divine protection from magic, the evil eye, and subtle nocturnal harms.

references.text: Every night when the Prophet went to bed, he would cup his hands together and blow into them after reciting Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas, then wipe his hands over whatever he could of his body, starting with his head and face, doing so three times.

deeds.name: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas (10 Times)
deeds.description: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas ten times in a day.
howToDo: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112) ten times, in one sitting or spread through the day.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Earns a palace built by Allah in Jannah and affirms core monotheism (Tawhid).

references.text: Whoever recites Qul huwa Allahu ahad ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is equivalent to a third of the Qur'an.

deeds.name: Recite Last 2 Ayat of Surah Al-Baqarah
deeds.description: Recite the final two verses of Al-Baqarah before sleeping.
howToDo: Recite verses 285 and 286 of Surah Al-Baqarah before going to sleep.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Serves as complete protection for the night and counts as spending the night in devotion.

references.text: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.
The last two verses of Al-Baqarah were given to the Prophet from a treasure beneath the Throne.

deeds.name: Memorizing 1 New Ayah
deeds.description: Memorize one new verse of the Qur'an each day.
howToDo: Repeat a new verse until it is fully memorized.
Understand its meaning and review it during optional prayers.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Elevates spiritual status in Paradise and permanently preserves divine light within.

references.text: It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an: Recite and ascend, and recite as you used to recite in the world, for your rank will be at the last verse you recite.
The one who is proficient in the Qur'an will be with the noble, righteous scribes.

deeds.name: Revision / Muraja'ah of Qur'an
deeds.description: Review previously memorized portions to prevent forgetting.
howToDo: Systematically review previously memorized surahs or pages.
Repeat until the recall is confident, to prevent forgetfulness.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Protects sacred knowledge from slipping away and keeps the mind continuously tied to revelation.

references.text: The example of the one who recites the Qur'an and memorizes it is like the owner of tied camels: if he keeps holding them, he keeps them, and if he releases them, they go away.

deeds.name: Reciting 100 Ayat in Night Prayer
deeds.description: Recite 100 or more verses during night prayer.
howToDo: During Tahajjud or Qiyam al-Layl, recite verses until reaching a total of 100 or more.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Protects from being recorded among the negligent and places one among the devout.

references.text: Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night will not be recorded among the negligent.

deeds.name: Fasting the Month of Ramadan
deeds.description: Abstain from food, drink, and relations from dawn to sunset throughout Ramadan.
howToDo: Abstain from food, drink, and marital relations from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib) every day of Ramadan.
Renew your intention each night and maintain good conduct and worship throughout the fast.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Fulfills the fourth pillar of Islam, expiates past minor sins, and builds sustained God-consciousness.

references.text: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous.

deeds.name: Fasting Mondays and Thursdays
deeds.description: Fast every Monday and Thursday from dawn until Maghrib.
howToDo: Fast from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib) every Monday and Thursday.
Make the intention the night before, or any time before midday if needed.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Ensures your weekly deeds are presented to Allah while you are in a state of worship.

references.text: Deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and I like for my deeds to be presented while I am fasting.

deeds.name: Fasting the White Days (Ayyam al-Beed)
deeds.description: Fast on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of every Islamic lunar month.
howToDo: Fast on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of every Islamic lunar month.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Multiplies rewards tenfold, making three days of monthly fasting equal to perpetual reward.

references.text: The Prophet said to me: O Abu Dharr, if you fast three days of the month, then fast the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the fifteenth.

deeds.name: Fasting the Day of Arafah
deeds.description: Fast on the 9th day of Dhul-Hijjah if not performing Hajj.
howToDo: Fast on the 9th day of Dhul-Hijjah, the Day of Arafah, if you are not performing Hajj.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Wipes away two full years of minor sins - the past year and the upcoming year.

references.text: Fasting the day of Arafah, I hope, expiates for the year before it and the year after it.

deeds.name: Fasting Ashura & Tasu'a
deeds.description: Fast the 10th of Muharram, preferably paired with the 9th.
howToDo: Fast the 10th of Muharram (Ashura).
Pair it with a fast on the 9th (Tasu'a) to differ from other communities.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Expiates the minor sins of the past year and commemorates Allah saving Prophet Musa (AS).

references.text: Fasting the day of Ashura, I hope that Allah will accept it as expiation for the year that came before it.

deeds.name: Fasting 6 Days of Shawwal
deeds.description: Fast any 6 days during the lunar month of Shawwal after Eid al-Fitr.
howToDo: Fast any 6 days during the month of Shawwal, after completing Ramadan and celebrating Eid al-Fitr.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Yields the continuous reward of a full year of fasting when paired with Ramadan.

references.text: Whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime.

deeds.name: Fasting in the Month of Muharram
deeds.description: Observe voluntary fasts throughout the sacred month of Muharram.
howToDo: Observe voluntary fasts on any days throughout the sacred month of Muharram.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Secures the most virtuous voluntary fasts outside of Ramadan and honors Allah's sacred month.

references.text: The best fasting after Ramadan is fasting in the month of Allah, Muharram.

deeds.name: Fasting during Sha'ban
deeds.description: Fast frequently throughout the month of Sha'ban preceding Ramadan.
howToDo: Fast frequently throughout the month of Sha'ban in preparation for Ramadan.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Prepares the soul for Ramadan and ensures annual deeds are raised while you are in worship.

references.text: The Messenger of Allah used to fast until we thought he would never stop, and he would leave off fasting until we thought he would never fast; and I never saw him fast a complete month except Ramadan, nor did I see him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.

deeds.name: Fasting First 9 Days of Dhul-Hijjah
deeds.description: Fast during any or all of the first nine days of Dhul-Hijjah.
howToDo: Fast on any or all of the first nine days of Dhul-Hijjah, the most virtuous days of the year.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Maximizes rewards during the most sacred and virtuous ten days of the Islamic calendar.

references.text: There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days.

deeds.name: Fasting of Dawud (Alternate Days)
deeds.description: Fast every other day consistently, without neglecting health or family rights.
howToDo: Fast every alternate day, breaking your fast the following day.
Maintain the pattern consistently without neglecting your health or the rights of your family.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Represents the highest level of voluntary fasting, most beloved to Allah.

references.text: The most beloved fasting to Allah was the fasting of Dawud; he used to fast every alternate day.

deeds.name: Making Up Missed Fast (Qada)
deeds.description: Fast on any permissible day before the next Ramadan to make up missed obligatory days.
howToDo: Fast on any permissible day before the following Ramadan begins, to make up each day missed.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Fulfills a compulsory debt owed to Allah and removes accountability for missed fasts.

references.text: And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days.

deeds.name: Fasting in the Sacred Months (Al-Ashhur Al-Hurum)
deeds.description: Observe voluntary fasts during Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab.
howToDo: Observe voluntary fasts on any days during the four sacred months: Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Elevates good deeds during periods specially sanctified by Allah.

references.text: Fast some days of the sacred month, then leave off.

deeds.name: Expiation Fasting (Kaffarah)
deeds.description: Fast consecutive required days, such as 3 days for a broken oath, as prescribed by Sharia.
howToDo: Fast the number of consecutive days prescribed by Sharia for the specific violation, such as 3 days for a broken oath.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Atones for broken solemn oaths and deliberate religious violations.

references.text: But whoever cannot find [or afford it] - then a fast of three days.

deeds.name: Fasting for Unmarried Youth
deeds.description: Fast voluntarily when unable to marry, to control physical desires and guard chastity.
howToDo: Fast voluntarily whenever unable to marry, to help control physical desire and guard chastity.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Acts as a spiritual shield against temptation and builds self-mastery.

references.text: O young men, whoever among you can afford marriage, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards chastity. And whoever cannot, let him fast, for it is a shield for him.

deeds.name: Fasting of a Vow (Nadhr)
deeds.description: Fast the specific number of days pledged to Allah upon fulfillment of a condition.
howToDo: Fast the exact number of days you pledged to Allah once the condition of your vow has been fulfilled.
deeds.benefitsAndVirtue: Fulfills a binding religious covenant made directly with Allah.

references.text: ...and let them fulfill their vows.
